summary: In this initiation lecture Indradyumna Swami explains that initiation is always auspicious, because auspiciousness means coming closer to Krishna, and through initiation the disciple firmly commits to surrender to Krishna's representative by chanting sixteen rounds, following the four regulative principles, associating with devotees, and serving the sankirtana movement. He describes the relationship as a reciprocal contract: the disciple vows aloud while the spiritual master silently vows in his heart to take responsibility for delivering that sincere disciple back to Godhead. This is illustrated by the story of Tamal Krishna Goswami, who, though living in Vrindavan while managing the difficult construction of the Krishna-Balaram Mandir, complained that amid the poor-quality cement, corruption and lazy workers he could not remember Krishna; Prabhupada assured him that if he simply continued serving his spiritual master, Lord Chaitanya would personally appear at the time of death and carry him back to Godhead. The Swami retells Prabhupada's beach analogy of two kinds of dogs, dirty quarreling strays with no master versus clean happy pedigree dogs on a leash, to teach that the soul who accepts and serves a bona fide guru is protected and cared for, while the one who wanders independently lives only on his own fate. He stresses that the living being is eternally a servant by nature and is happy only when serving guru and Krishna, that pure service seeks no reward but only more service, and that Krishna, feeling indebted, reciprocates by giving His devotees the most valuable gift of more devotional service, as He did with the gopis. He assures the initiates that whatever they need, materially and spiritually, will be supplied if they remain fully surrendered, sharing his own story of receiving a US Social Security letter promising him only $16.43 yet feeling no anxiety because Krishna has always maintained him and given him far more than he could have hoped for. The essence, he concludes, is one-pointed service to Guru and Gauranga, humbly inquiring, learning and applying transcendental knowledge, and then sharing it with others, so that one may become a genuine Vaishnava.
key_points: Initiation is always auspicious because auspiciousness means drawing closer to Krishna; the disciple's vows (16 rounds, four regulative principles, association with devotees, service to the sankirtana movement) are reciprocated by the guru's responsibility to deliver him.

On the path of jnana or yoga success depends on one's own effort, but on the path of bhakti the spiritual master, our eternal well-wisher (as Prabhupada always signed his letters), takes responsibility to bring the disciple back to Godhead.

Every living being is a servant by constitution; we serve either the material energy (senses, mind, selfish desires) or Krishna, and only serving guru and Krishna brings real happiness because it is our natural position.

Quality, pure service asks for no reward; the only thing worth desiring is more service. Krishna, feeling indebted to His devotees, reciprocates by giving them more devotional service, as He did with the gopis who abandoned everything to come to Him.
For a fully surrendered devotee Krishna personally provides what is lacking and preserves what he has; the sacrifice (yajna) and even the material facilities to perform it come by God's grace.

The guru-disciple relationship is to approach humbly, inquire, render service, receive knowledge and apply it, then preach it, following the example of Mahaprabhu, who preached daily, and Prabhupada, who spread the holy name worldwide.

Cleanliness is next to godliness and is a requirement for second initiation, because only one who is internally clean can fix the mind on Krishna, who is suddha-sattva, completely pure and transcendental.
references: Sikshastakam, verse 4 (Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu) - 'na dhanam na janam na sundarim kavitam va jagad-isa kamaye... mama janmani janmani isvare bhavatad bhaktir ahaituki tvayi': I desire no wealth, followers, beautiful women or fame, only causeless devotional service to Your lotus feet birth after birth. Cited to illustrate the mood of pure surrender.
Bhagavad-gita 9.2 - 'raja-vidya raja-guhyam': Krishna consciousness is the king of knowledge and the king of secrets, the priceless gift of divine knowledge the guru bestows.

Bhagavad-gita 4.34 - 'tad viddhi pranipatena pariprasnena sevaya': approach a spiritual master, inquire submissively and render service, and the self-realized souls will impart knowledge. The Swami presents it as Krishna's own most important instruction, to be kept on the tip of the tongue as the essence of the guru-disciple relationship.

Bhagavad-gita 3.10 - at the beginning of creation Krishna sent forth generations of men and demigods and blessed them that by the performance of yajna (sacrifice) all they require would be provided; cited to show that material and spiritual prosperity come by God's grace.
Bhagavad-gita 9.22 - 'yoga-kshemam vahamy aham': for His devotee the Lord carries what he lacks and preserves what he has; the master provides and protects everything the surrendered servant needs.

Chanakya Pandit (Chanakya-niti) - verse praising knowledge as the supreme ornament: 'the ornament of the night is the moon, the ornament of a woman is a good husband, the ornament of the earth is the king, and knowledge is the ornament of all'; cited on the value of both material and spiritual knowledge. Exact verse number not identified.

Srimad Bhagavatam, First Canto - said by Prabhupada to contain the complete science of Krishna consciousness ('even shipwrecked on a lonely island you could become fully Krishna conscious just by reading the First Canto'). The Swami also alludes generally to a statement in the later cantos that the spiritual master takes responsibility to bring back a disciple who enthusiastically serves the sankirtana mission; exact verse not identified, so not guessed.
stories: Tamal Krishna Goswami's complaint — managing the Krishna-Balaram Mandir amid corruption, poor cement and lazy workers, he could not remember Krishna; Prabhupada assured him that if he kept serving, Lord Chaitanya would personally carry him back at death.

The two kinds of dogs — on the beach Prabhupada contrasts dirty, quarreling masterless strays with clean, happy pedigree dogs on a leash, to show that the soul who accepts a guru is protected and cared for.
Prabhupada cleaning the floor — seeing Yamuna Dasi cleaning wrongly, he got on his hands and knees with the same bucket and rag to show her how.
The 16.43 dollar Social Security letter — expecting thousands, the Swami's retirement statement promised only 16.43 dollars, yet he felt no anxiety, trusting Krishna to maintain him.
Krishna indebted to the gopis — unable to repay the gopis who abandoned everything at his flute, Krishna gives them the most valuable gift: more service.
The Lakshmis cleaning Vaikuntha's pillars — the goddesses of fortune happily clean dust-free pillars out of sheer eagerness to serve.
Prabhupada 'just trying to become a Vaishnava' — praised as the greatest Vaishnava, he replied that a Vaishnava is a very special thing and he was only trying to become one.
The book-bag life — the Swami says he would happily return to France, fill his old bag with books and wander distributing them door to door, sleeping in the sankirtana van.
quotes: For my devotee I protect whatever they have and I provide whatever they need.
We're all servants, but we want to offer quality service.
A Vaishnava is a very special thing. I'm just trying to become a Vaishnava.
